name: Checking How Well Models Handle Multimodal Content
gist: Papers develop tests for how models work with mixed inputs like text plus images, videos, audio, tables, and graphs — ensuring they can coordinate information across different types of data.
explain: Real-world information is messy and mixed. A news article might come with photos. A scientific paper has text, equations, graphs, and images. A video has sound and motion and visuals. A table of data is a different kind of input than a paragraph. This subtheme is about building tests for how AI models handle information that mixes different types together—multimodal content.

The challenge is that handling mixed types requires coordination. A model has to read text, understand images, parse graphs, listen to audio, and then combine all of that to answer a question or complete a task. It is not enough for a model to be great at images and also great at text if it cannot connect them. A model might see a photo and read a caption but completely miss how they relate. It might misunderstand the scale of a graph or fail to notice that the text contradicts the visual data. Building tests for this coordination is hard because you have to measure whether a model genuinely integrated information across modes or just processed each mode separately and guessed a combined answer.

Researchers build multimodal benchmarks by gathering data that naturally mixes types. Some focus on videos with sound and visual understanding. Others test models on documents with mixed text and images, like research papers or web pages. Still others create specific tasks that require coordination: "based on this table and this description, what is the answer?" or "watch this video and this happens; describe the next second." The goal is to measure whether models can truly work with mixed information, which is essential as AI moves toward handling real-world tasks.

papers.title: $PhyWorldBench$: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Physical Realism in Text-to-Video Models
papers.contribution: Evaluations across 1,050 prompts show state-of-the-art models still fail to adhere to real-world physics, identifying pivotal challenges in physics realism.

papers.title: A Very Big Video Reasoning Suite
papers.contribution: Scaling studies on VBVR observe early signs of emergent generalization to unseen reasoning tasks; dataset and benchmark tools released publicly.

papers.title: Battery Fault: A Comprehensive Dataset and Benchmark for Battery Fault Diagnosis
papers.contribution: Provides large-scale real-world EV battery fault diagnosis dataset supporting classification and grading tasks with baseline results from RF, SVM, LSTM, and CNN models.

papers.title: CounselBench: A Large-Scale Expert Evaluation and Adversarial Benchmarking of Large Language Models in Mental Health Question Answering
papers.contribution: Expert evaluation reveals LLMs achieve high scores on several dimensions but exhibit recurring issues including unconstructive feedback, overgeneralization, limited personalization, and safety risks like unauthorized medical advice.

papers.title: HumanPCR: Probing MLLM Capabilities in Diverse Human-Centric Scenes
papers.contribution: Extensive evaluation of 30+ state-of-the-art models reveals significant challenges in human-centric visual understanding, especially in spatial perception, temporal understanding, and mind modeling.

papers.title: M4PQA: A Comprehensive QA Dataset for AI Research with Instance-Level Evaluation
papers.contribution: Demonstrates most models underperform M4PQA; ExTrActor consistently improves small models' tool-use capability to match larger models while enabling instance-level evaluation.

papers.title: MedAraBench: Large-scale Arabic Medical Question Answering Dataset and Benchmark
papers.contribution: Provides large-scale Arabic medical QA benchmark spanning 19 specialties and five difficulty levels to broaden medical AI evaluation diversity.

papers.title: Same Content, Different Representations: A Controlled Study for Table QA
papers.contribution: Reveals consistent trade-offs: SQL excels on structured data, LLMs provide flexibility with reduced precision, and hybrids strike balance particularly under noisy schemas.

papers.title: AVTrack: Audio-Visual Tracking in Human-centric Complex Scenes
papers.contribution: Reveals substantial performance degradation of existing methods and establishes AVTrack as a challenging benchmark for robust audio-visual scene understanding in dynamic environments.

papers.title: AtelierEval: Agentic Evaluation of Humans & LLMs as Text-to-Image Prompters
papers.contribution: Achieves 0.79 Spearman correlation with human experts; benchmarks 8 MLLMs against 48 humans across 4 T2I backends, revealing superiority of mimicry over planning.

papers.title: ChemEval: A Multi-level and Fine-grained Chemical Capability Evaluation for Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Evaluates mainstream LLMs showing general-purpose models excel at chemical literature understanding but lack deep expertise, while chemical LLMs struggle with general language.

papers.title: CoDA: From Text-to-Image Diffusion Models to Training-Free Dataset Distillation
papers.contribution: Achieves performance on par with or better than target-specific distillation methods across ImageNet-1K and subsets without requiring target-specific training.

papers.title: DrivingGen: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Generative Video World Models in Autonomous Driving
papers.contribution: Benchmarking 14 state-of-the-art models reveals clear trade-offs: general models look better but break physics while driving-specific ones capture motion realistically but lag in visual quality.

papers.title: FRABench and UFEval: Unified Fine-grained Evaluation with Task and Aspect Generalization
papers.contribution: First unified fine-grained evaluator with task and aspect generalization achieving 60.4k pairwise samples with 325k labels for multimodal evaluation.

papers.title: From Natural Alignment to Conditional Controllability in Multimodal Dialogue
papers.contribution: Demonstrates current frameworks' limitations in replicating human interaction expressiveness and provides benchmark for style-controllable dialogue.

papers.title: GIR-Bench: Versatile Benchmark for Generating Images with Reasoning
papers.contribution: GIR-Bench reveals that unified models remain persistently behind on reasoning-driven visual generation despite being more capable than generation-only systems, identifying a key performance gap.

papers.title: GenExam: A Multidisciplinary Text-to-Image Exam
papers.contribution: Reveals large gap between open-source and closed-source models, providing rigorous assessment of integrated understanding, reasoning, and generation.

papers.title: How Well Does GPT-4o Understand Vision? Evaluating Multimodal Foundation Models on Standard Computer Vision Tasks
papers.contribution: Shows models are not close to specialist models but perform better on semantic tasks than geometric ones, with GPT-4o securing top position in 4 of 6 tasks among non-reasoning models.

papers.title: Measuring Audio's Impact on Correctness: Audio-Contribution-Aware Post-Training of Large Audio Language Models
papers.contribution: Achieves first place in DCASE 2025 Audio-Question-Answering challenge and 78.2% on MMAU-test set.

papers.title: OmniWorld: A Multi-Domain and Multi-Modal Dataset for 4D World Modeling
papers.contribution: Fine-tuning existing methods on OmniWorld leads to significant performance gains on 4D reconstruction and video generation tasks, validating it as a powerful resource.

papers.title: On Path to Multimodal Historical Reasoning: HistBench and HistAgent
papers.contribution: HistAgent achieves 28.50% pass@1 and 36.47% pass@2 on HistBench, significantly outperforming GPT-4o, DeepSeek-R1, and other generalist agents.

papers.title: PCB-Bench: Benchmarking LLMs for Printed Circuit Board Placement and Routing
papers.contribution: Benchmarking 23 LLM variants reveals substantial gaps in reasoning over spatial placements, following domain-specific constraints, and interpreting professional engineering artifacts.

papers.title: Privasis: Synthesizing the Largest "Public" Private Dataset from Scratch
papers.contribution: Compact sanitization models (≤4B) trained on Privasis outperform large models like GPT-5 and Qwen-3 235B.

papers.title: PuzzleWorld: A Benchmark for Multimodal, Open-Ended Reasoning in Puzzlehunts
papers.contribution: Best models achieve only 14% accuracy and 40% stepwise accuracy, matching novices but failing enthusiasts; fine-tuning on traces improves downstream tasks.

papers.title: T2AV-Compass: Towards Unified Evaluation for Text-to-Audio-Video Generation
papers.contribution: First comprehensive benchmark for T2AV systems showing even strongest models fall substantially short of human-level realism and cross-modal consistency.

papers.title: TopBench: A Benchmark for Implicit Predictive Reasoning in Tabular Question Answering
papers.contribution: Reveals current models struggle with intent recognition and accurate intent disambiguation serves as prerequisite for predictive behaviors.

papers.title: TrustGen: A Platform of Dynamic Benchmarking on the Trustworthiness of Generative Foundation Models
papers.contribution: Evaluating 39 models reveals that state-of-the-art GenFMs achieve promising overall trust but have significant limitations in hallucination resistance, fairness, and privacy preservation.

papers.title: WISE: World Knowledge-Informed Semantic Evaluation for Text-to-Image Generation
papers.contribution: Reveals significant limitations in 20 models (10 dedicated T2I and 10 unified multimodal) regarding ability to effectively integrate and apply world knowledge.

papers.title: XModBench: Benchmarking Cross-Modal Capabilities and Consistency in Omni-Language Models
papers.contribution: Even Gemini-2.5-Pro struggles with spatial/temporal reasoning (<60% accuracy) and exhibits 20+ point modality disparities and directional imbalance.
